options: Creates a Windows Task Scheduler entry entirely from PowerShell, without using the Task Scheduler GUI
Registers a new SQL Server Agent job
Creates a new dbatools module
Schedules a T-SQL query inside SSMS only

questions.q: How does schtasks.exe relate to Register-ScheduledTask?
options: It's the older command-line equivalent, predating the ScheduledTasks module, that creates the same underlying Task Scheduler entry
It is a completely unrelated Linux-only tool
It only works with SQL Server Agent, not Task Scheduler
It has been fully removed from modern Windows versions

questions.q: What is the real permission limitation of running a PowerShell step inside a SQL Server Agent job?
options: It runs under the single SQL Server Agent service account for every job, not a dedicated account chosen per script
SQL Server Agent cannot run PowerShell steps at all
Agent jobs can only run once per day
PowerShell steps in Agent jobs cannot access dbatools
questions.explain: Every PowerShell step across every Agent job shares the same fixed service account, which is either under- or over-privileged for a given script's actual needs.

questions.q: What does Windows Task Scheduler offer that addresses SQL Server Agent's PowerShell-step account limitation?
options: The ability to specify exactly which dedicated account each individual scheduled task runs under
Automatic elevation to sysadmin for every task
No accounts are needed at all in Task Scheduler
It removes the need for any error handling in the script
questions.explain: Task Scheduler lets each task run under its own scoped account rather than sharing one fixed account across every job.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why is a dedicated service account preferred over a personal admin account for scheduled DBA scripts?
options: A personal account breaks when that person changes their password or leaves the team, and using an over-privileged shared account violates least-privilege principles
Personal accounts are technically incapable of running scheduled tasks
Dedicated service accounts run scripts faster
There is no real difference; either works equally well long-term
questions.explain: A scoped, dedicated service account is stable and limited to exactly what each script needs, unlike a personal account tied to one person's employment and credentials.
